label: Holy hour
blurb: The chapel at six, before anyone. The Blessed Sacrament does not talk back, which is the point.

label: Study
blurb: The library after supper, the reading that was assigned and the reading that was not.

label: Spiritual direction
blurb: An hour a week with the man who will know you better than the rector does, and say less.

label: Parish weekend
blurb: Saturday and Sunday at a parish: the sacristy, the sick list, the coffee after.
digest: the sick list and the coffee after

label: Basketball and the gym
blurb: The gym at four, the court behind the dorm, and the men you cannot beat.

label: The common room
blurb: Cards, the game on, the argument about the professor. Where the class becomes a class.

label: Spanish
blurb: The language half the diocese prays in. Forty hours to say Mass in it badly; a lifetime to say it well.

credentialAfter.line: You can hear confessions in Spanish now, slowly. The diocese will notice.

label: Latin
blurb: The Church's own tongue, and a door to the older books and the older Mass.

credentialAfter.line: You can read the Latin now, and the older men have noticed you can.

digest: Latin, and a psalm learned by heart

label: Sacristan
blurb: Student leadership: the vestments, the candles, the rector's eye. Small, and the rector notices.

label: Writing
blurb: The essay nobody assigned, the letter to the paper, the journal. A voice starts here.
digest: a letter you did not send

label: Italian
blurb: The language of the Gregorian's lectures and the Curia's corridors. Sixty hours to follow a lecture; the rector notices who is taking them, and so does the bishop when a place in Rome comes open.

credentialAfter.line: You can follow a lecture in Italian now, and the rector has put a note in your file that the bishop will read when Rome comes up.

digest: Italian tapes in the language lab
an Italian newspaper read with a dictionary

label: French
blurb: The language of the Haitians and the Africans in the pews, of half the older theology, and of Lourdes. Sixty hours to preach in it; the parishes with a Creole Mass will ask for you.

credentialAfter.line: You can preach in French now, to the Haitians and the Africans and the one Québécois family, and read the older theology in it.

digest: French tapes in the language lab
a Bernanos novel read with a dictionary

label: German
blurb: The language of Ratzinger and Rahner in the original, and of the old families who still want a Christmas Mass in it. Sixty hours to read a page; the professors notice who can.

credentialAfter.line: You can read Ratzinger in German now, and say Mass for the old families at Christmas.

digest: a page of Ratzinger with a dictionary

label: Polish
blurb: The language of a third of the old parishes and of the grandmothers who have not confessed in it for twenty years. Seventy hours to say the Gorzkie żale.

credentialAfter.line: You can say the Gorzkie żale now and hear a grandmother's confession in Polish, which she has waited twenty years for.

digest: the Gorzkie żale learned by heart

label: Vietnamese
blurb: Six tones and a community that will forgive you every one of them for trying. Eighty hours to say their Mass; a lifetime to hear a confession in it.

credentialAfter.line: The tones took a year and the community took a month to stop laughing kindly. You can say their Mass now.

label: Tagalog
blurb: The language of the Filipino Mass and the Santo Niño, and of half the nurses in the hospital. Sixty hours to preach in it, badly and to applause.

credentialAfter.line: You can preach in Tagalog now, badly and to applause, and the Santo Niño Mass is yours.

digest: a Tagalog hymn learned by ear

label: Korean
blurb: The language of the Korean Mass and the catechists' meetings. Eighty hours to say the Mass and follow the meeting, most of it.

credentialAfter.line: You can say the Korean Mass now and follow the catechists' meeting, most of it.

digest: a Korean grammar, and a headache

label: The rite of the order
blurb: The crypt chapel with the old friar who still says it: the chalice prepared at the start, the short Confiteor, the arms. An hour a week for a year and you can say it, by leave, when you are a priest.

credentialAfter.line: You can say the rite of the order now, slowly and without error, and the old friar has said so to the master of students. When you are a priest it will be yours to ask leave for.

digest: An hour in the crypt with the old man and the card of responses.
The chalice at the start, again, until your hands know it.
The arms, held, in the empty chapel with the lights off.
